caption: The drawing consists of three overlapping rectangular patterns resembling woven textile samples, each contained within thin black borders. The patterns use a palette of muted earth tones, primarily beige, brown, cream, and gray, with darker elements in black or deep blue. The two larger rectangles are positioned vertically along the left and bottom sides of the composition, both featuring complex geometric designs formed by repeating square and rectangular blocks, circles, diamonds, and tinier checkerboard motifs. The central upper rectangle is set atop the other two and slightly overlaps them, displaying a denser and slightly darker iteration of the woven design, with a prominent central square filled with a dense checkerboard pattern. The background of the drawing is a light, off-white color with occasional small orange-brown stains. The patterns are composed of repeated geometric shapes with alternating colors creating textured, detailed surfaces. At the bottom right, there is a handwritten name: "Manuel G. Runyan".
title: Woven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
